title_guess: India's forex reserves: what they hold and where they stand (RBI weekly data, July 2024)
running_examples: total reserves about $667.4 bn on 26 Jul 2024, near the all-time high of about $670 bn, enough for about 11 months of imports
reserves grew from about $1.8 bn (1951-52) to $607 bn (2021-22): 335x since independence, 60x since the 1990s; fourth largest in the world (Nov 2021)

best_moments.why: India's map carries a vault of lockers, followed by an equals sign and the four parts stacked as a sum: the reserve is literally a vault made of four things
a bracket joins the four shaded component rows up to the total row: parts add up to the whole on the real data table
a tiny money bag at the start of the growth curve and a huge one at the end make the 335x growth felt without reading numbers

weak_moments.why: screenshot of a web list of weekly reports in tiny unreadable text
full data table screenshot with many columns before it is cut down
borrowed government factsheet image with official logos instead of an own drawing

segments.teaches: forex reserves = foreign currency assets + gold + SDRs + reserve tranche position in the IMF

elements.what: India silhouette with a block of locker doors (vault) on it
FOREX RESERVE =
four components stacked with + signs
green rising bar chart with a pointer label 'data' (from ~15 s)

segments.notes: the rising bar icon is a promise of numbers to come; the vault/locker icon is the same forex-reserve icon used in E22
segments.idea: India's forex reserve is a store made of four parts: foreign currency, gold, SDRs and its IMF reserve position
segments.shown_as: India's silhouette with a block of vault lockers on it, an equals sign, and four components stacked like a sum (foreign currency + gold + SDRs + reserve tranche); then a green rising bar chart pops above with a pointer saying data

segments.teaches: the current figures come from RBI's weekly reports on its website; open the latest one to see the reserves table

elements.what: RBI logo and highlighted web address
screenshot of a list of dated weekly forex reports
green box on the top row with a 'latest report' label
screenshot of the report's table (total and four components, with week / end-March / year change columns)
blue wash on the change columns before they are cut away

segments.notes: screen capture of a real source page; it teaches the learner where to look the data up
segments.idea: the RBI publishes the reserve figures every week; the latest report gives the current position
segments.shown_as: an RBI logo and web address appear over a screenshot of a long list of dated weekly reports; the top row is boxed in green as the latest report; below it the report's table appears and its change columns are washed in blue before being cut away

segments.teaches: on 26 July 2024 total reserves were about $667 bn, near the all-time high of about $670 bn and enough for about 11 months of imports; the four components add up to the total

elements.what: table cut down to the 'as on' columns (₹ crore, US$ million), five rows
yellow band on the total-reserves row
black tag converting the total to about 667 billion USD
italic note: all-time high near 670 billion in July
cloud bubble: covers about 11 months of imports
purple band on the four component rows with a bracket up to the total

segments.notes: unit conversion (US$ million -> billion) done for the viewer in a tag
segments.idea: India holds about $667 bn of reserves, close to its record, enough to pay for about 11 months of imports
segments.shown_as: the table zooms to just the 'as on' columns; the total row is boxed in yellow, a black tag converts it to about 667 billion dollars, an italic note adds the all-time high near 670 billion, a cloud bubble says it covers about 11 months of imports, and finally a bracket joins the four purple-shaded component rows up to the total
segments.example: $667.4 bn total on 26 Jul 2024; ~11 months of import cover

segments.teaches: reserves rose from about $1.8 bn in 1951-52 to $607 bn in 2021-22 (335x since independence, 60x since the 1990s); India had the fourth-largest reserves (Nov 2021)

elements.what: government press-bureau factsheet header with official logos
line chart by decade from 1951-52 to 2021-22: flat until 1991-92 then shooting up to 607
tiny money bag at the start and a large rupee money bag at the end of the line
yellow tag: 60x rise since the 1990s
green rising bars icon with a note: fourth largest reserves (Nov 2021)

segments.notes: borrowed official chart; BIE should redraw its own curve and money bags
segments.idea: India's reserves were tiny for 40 years and have grown hugely since the 1990s
segments.shown_as: a factsheet chart: a line of decade dots stays flat from 1951 to 1991 and then shoots up to 607; a tiny money bag at the start and a huge rupee money bag at the end make the growth visible; a yellow tag says 60x since the 1990s, then the view pulls back and a green rising-bars icon carries a note about being fourth largest in the world
segments.example: $1.82 bn (1951-52) -> $607 bn (2021-22); 335x since independence; 60x since the 1990s
